    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)

    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]

    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)

    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false

    13	  // bool is a subtype of int: a Bool compared with an Int promotes to 0/1 and
    14	  // re-dispatches to the Int comparison cases (True==1, False==0, True<2, ...).

    16	  // promoted for Bool x Bool (to avoid duplicating the two rules above).

    18	       requires isEqOrdOp(OP)
    19	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, I:Int, B:Bool) => applyCmp(OP, I, boolAsInt(B))
    20	       requires isEqOrdOp(OP)
    21	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => applyCmp(OP, boolAsInt(B1), boolAsInt(B2))
    22	       requires isOrdOp(OP)
    23	
    24	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================

    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>

    33	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    34	       requires truthy(V)

    36	       requires notBool truthy(V)

    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/functions.k — MPY-FUNCTIONS
     2	
     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/builtins.k — MPY-BUILTINS

     3	module MPY-BUILTINS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-STR
     6	  imports MPY-SET
     7	  imports MPY-ITER
     8	  imports MPY-RANGE
     9	  imports MPY-INT
    10	  imports MPY-METHODS
    11	
    12	  // the builtins REGISTRY is core.k's builtinsScope (the -1 frame); names resolve by lookup
    13	
    14	  // Call routing + argument evaluation live in call.k, which also routes the fold
    15	  // builtins (sum/all/any/max/min) to the #_Acc folds below and everything else to
    16	  // applyBuiltin. This module owns applyBuiltin + the fold implementations.
    17	  syntax Val ::= applyBuiltin(String, Vals) [function]
    18	
    19	  // ==== len(obj) — O(1) per kind ============================================
    20	  syntax Int ::= seqLen(Val) [function]
    21	  rule applyBuiltin("len", OBJ:Val, .Vals) => seqLen(OBJ)
    22	  rule seqLen(list(VS:ValSeq))                  => vsLen(VS)
    23	  rule seqLen(tuple(VS:ValSeq))                 => vsLen(VS)
    24	  rule seqLen(str(IS:IntSeq))                   => isLen(IS)
    25	  rule seqLen(setV(DS:IntSeq))                  => isLen(DS)
    26	  rule seqLen(rangeObj(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => rangeLen(LO, HI, ST)
    27	
    28	  // ==== list(seq) — materialize a list/tuple into a list (e.g. list(d.keys())) ==
    29	  // Minimal: the "copy a sequence" case (list of a list is itself; list of a tuple keeps order).
    30	  // list() of other iterables (str/range/set/zip) is added via the iterator fold when needed.
    31	  // (k-cell — list() constructs a NEW object)
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (list(VS:ValSeq),  .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
    33	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (tuple(VS:ValSeq), .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
    34	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), .Vals)                     => #alloc(list(.ValSeq)) ... </k>
    35	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals))   => #alloc(list(charsOf(CS))) ... </k>
    36	  syntax ValSeq ::= charsOf(IntSeq) [function, total]
    37	  rule charsOf(.IntSeq)                => .ValSeq
    38	  rule charsOf(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => vCons(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), charsOf(R))
    39	
    40	  // ==== set(str) — distinct character codes =================================
    41	  rule applyBuiltin("set", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => setV(dedupCodes(CS))
    42	
    43	  // ==== abs(int) ============================================================
    44	  rule applyBuiltin("abs", I:Int, .Vals) => absInt(I)
    45	
    46	  // ==== sum(iterable) — one #iterNext fold; intOf = int value of an int/bool ==
    47	  syntax KItem ::= #sumAcc(Iterable, Int) | #sumCont(Int)
    48	  rule <k> #sumAcc(IT:Iterable, ACC:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumCont(ACC) ... </k>
    49	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int) => ACC ... </k>
    50	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
    51	        => #sumAcc(R, ACC +Int intOf(V)) ... </k>
    52	       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)
    53	
    54	  syntax Int ::= intOf(Val) [function]
    55	  rule intOf(I:Int)  => I
    56	  rule intOf(B:Bool) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    57	
    58	  // ==== all / any (short-circuiting #iterNext folds) ========================
    59	  syntax KItem ::= #allAcc(Iterable) | "#allCont"
    60	  rule <k> #allAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #allCont ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #allCont => true ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #allCont => #allAcc(R) ... </k>
    63	       requires truthy(V)
    64	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #allCont => false ... </k>
    65	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    66	
    67	  syntax KItem ::= #anyAcc(Iterable) | "#anyCont"
    68	  rule <k> #anyAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #anyCont ... </k>
    69	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #anyCont => false ... </k>
    70	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => true ... </k>
    71	       requires truthy(V)
    72	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => #anyAcc(R) ... </k>
    73	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    74	
    75	  // ==== max / min over an iterable (#iterNext folds; first element seeds) ====
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #maxAcc0(Iterable) | "#maxCont0" | #maxAcc(Iterable, Int) | #maxCont(Int)
    77	  rule <k> #maxAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont0 ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
    79	       requires isInt(V)
    80	  rule <k> #maxAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont(M) ... </k>
    81	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
    82	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont(M:Int)
    83	        => #maxAcc(R, maxInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
    84	       requires isInt(V)
    85	
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #minAcc0(Iterable) | "#minCont0" | #minAcc(Iterable, Int) | #minCont(Int)
    87	  rule <k> #minAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont0 ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
    89	       requires isInt(V)
    90	  rule <k> #minAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont(M) ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
    92	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont(M:Int)
    93	        => #minAcc(R, minInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
    94	       requires isInt(V)
    95	
    96	  // ---- general Val branch of the max/min folds (v3) ------------------------
    97	  // The Int fold above and the Float fold (float.k) cover homogeneous lists; the
    98	  // remaining CPython-orderable seeds (Bool, str) and every cross-sort step land
    99	  // here. Ordering reuses the semantics' OWN applyCmp dispatch (int.k; float.k's
   100	  // exact ltIF/ltFI bridges; bool.k's bool->int promotion; str.k's strLt), so
   101	  // mixed comparisons stay bit-exact with CPython; a pair applyCmp does not
   102	  // order (e.g. int vs str) leaves the fold stuck (unmodeled TypeError).
   103	  // Strict > (resp. <) replacement keeps the FIRST maximal (minimal) element —
   104	  // CPython's tie rule.
   105	  syntax KItem ::= #maxAccV(Iterable, Val) | #maxContV(Val)
   106	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAccV(R, V) ... </k>
   107	       requires isBool(V) orBool isStr(V)
   108	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont(M:Int)
   109	        => #iterYield(V, R) ~> #maxContV(M) ... </k>
   110	       requires isFloat(V) orBool isBool(V)
   111	  rule <k> #maxAccV(IT:Iterable, M:Val) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxContV(M) ... </k>
   112	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxContV(M:Val) => M ... </k>
   113	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxContV(M:Val) => #maxAccV(R, V) ... </k>
   114	       requires applyCmp(">", V, M)
   115	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxContV(M:Val) => #maxAccV(R, M) ... </k>
   116	       requires notBool applyCmp(">", V, M)
   117	
   118	  syntax KItem ::= #minAccV(Iterable, Val) | #minContV(Val)
   119	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAccV(R, V) ... </k>
   120	       requires isBool(V) orBool isStr(V)
   121	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont(M:Int)
   122	        => #iterYield(V, R) ~> #minContV(M) ... </k>
   123	       requires isFloat(V) orBool isBool(V)
   124	  rule <k> #minAccV(IT:Iterable, M:Val) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minContV(M) ... </k>
   125	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minContV(M:Val) => M ... </k>
   126	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minContV(M:Val) => #minAccV(R, V) ... </k>
   127	       requires applyCmp("<", V, M)
   128	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minContV(M:Val) => #minAccV(R, M) ... </k>
   129	       requires notBool applyCmp("<", V, M)
   130	
   131	  // ==== variadic max / min (a Vals fold) ====================================
   132	  // v3: Val operands (mixed int/float/bool, str) via the same applyCmp
   133	  // dispatch; strict > / < keeps the FIRST maximal/minimal operand (CPython's
   134	  // tie rule — and exactly the old maxInt/minInt fold on the all-Int domain).
   135	  syntax Val ::= maxVals(Val, Vals) [function]
   136	  rule applyBuiltin("max", I:Int, REST:Vals) => maxVals(I, REST)
   137	  rule applyBuiltin("max", V:Val, (V2:Val, REST:Vals)) => maxVals(V, (V2, REST))
   138	       requires isFloat(V) orBool isBool(V) orBool isStr(V)
   139	  rule maxVals(M:Val, .Vals)           => M
   140	  rule maxVals(M:Val, (V:Val, R:Vals)) => maxVals(V, R) requires applyCmp(">", V, M)
   141	  rule maxVals(M:Val, (V:Val, R:Vals)) => maxVals(M, R) requires notBool applyCmp(">", V, M)
   142	
   143	  syntax Val ::= minVals(Val, Vals) [function]
   144	  rule applyBuiltin("min", I:Int, REST:Vals) => minVals(I, REST)
   145	  rule applyBuiltin("min", V:Val, (V2:Val, REST:Vals)) => minVals(V, (V2, REST))
   146	       requires isFloat(V) orBool isBool(V) orBool isStr(V)
   147	  rule minVals(M:Val, .Vals)           => M
   148	  rule minVals(M:Val, (V:Val, R:Vals)) => minVals(V, R) requires applyCmp("<", V, M)
   149	  rule minVals(M:Val, (V:Val, R:Vals)) => minVals(M, R) requires notBool applyCmp("<", V, M)
   150	
   151	  // ==== bin(n) — "0b" + binary digit codes (promoted from 103's defined fold) ==
   152	  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals) => str(iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(N))))
   153	       requires N >=Int 0
   154	  // negative operand: the '-' sign prefixes the magnitude's digits
   155	  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals)
   156	    => str(iCons(45, iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(0 -Int N)))))
   157	       requires N <Int 0
   158	  syntax IntSeq ::= binCodes(Int) [function, total]
   159	  rule binCodes(0) => iCons(48, .IntSeq)

    86	  // (set.k needs no change: setV holds int char codes, compared with ==Int, so a
    87	  // cross-type ==K collapse never arises there.)
    88	  // krun-only (priority 40 beats list.k's default rules); kprove uses the
    89	  // structural ==K rules in list.k unchanged.
    90	  syntax Bool ::= numOrKEq(Val, Val) [function]
    91	  rule numOrKEq(A:Val, B:Val) => applyCmp("==", A, B)
    92	       requires (isInt(A) orBool isBool(A) orBool isFloat(A))
    93	        andBool (isInt(B) orBool isBool(B) orBool isFloat(B))
    94	  rule numOrKEq(A:Val, B:Val) => A ==K B [owise]
    95	
    96	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    97	       requires numOrKEq(E, V) [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    99	       requires notBool numOrKEq(E, V) [priority(40)]
   100	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

     3	module MPY-METHODS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports K-EQUAL
     6	  imports MPY-STR
     7	  imports MPY-LIST
     8	
     9	  // method-call routing + arg-eval live in call.k; this module owns applyMethod.
    10	  syntax Val ::= applyMethod(Val, String, Vals) [function]

    12	  // ==== string predicates (Python semantic…2592 tokens truncated…, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (ST >Int 0 andBool I <Int HI) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool I >Int HI)

    15	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (LO -Int HI -Int ST -Int 1) /Int (0 -Int ST)

     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule
FILE:sort.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
    24	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
    25	  // v3: mixed-numeric elements (float/bool heads; float/bool tail elements under
    26	  // an Int head) insert via the shared applyCmp dispatch — the exact ltIF/ltFI
    27	  // bridges (float.k) + the bool->int promotion (bool.k), so mixed sorts match
    28	  // CPython bit-exactly. X goes before Y iff not (Y < X) — the same tie rule as
    29	  // insVS's X <=Int Y, so equal keys keep first-seen order (stable insertion
    30	  // from the right). str-vs-numeric has no applyCmp leg and stays stuck
    31	  // (CPython TypeError).
    32	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSn(Val, ValSeq) [function]
    33	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Val, R:ValSeq)) => insVSn(X, sortVS(R))
    34	       requires isFloat(X) orBool isBool(X) [concrete]
    35	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R))
    36	       requires (isFloat(Y) orBool isBool(Y)) andBool notBool applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
    37	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R))
    38	       requires (isFloat(Y) orBool isBool(Y)) andBool applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
    39	  rule insVSn(X:Val, .ValSeq) => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    40	  rule insVSn(X:Val, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R))
    41	       requires notBool applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
    42	  rule insVSn(X:Val, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVSn(X, R))
    43	       requires applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
    44	  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
    45	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    46	  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    47	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
    48	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
    49	       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
    50	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
    51	       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]
    52	
    53	  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
    54	  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
    55	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
    56	        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>
    57	
    58	  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
    59	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
    60	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
    61	       [priority(40)]
    62	
    63	  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
    64	  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
    65	  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent checks of every proof-local definition and its guard coverage."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path


VERIFICATION = Path("/tmp/audit-work/reconstruction/verification.k")


def py_mod(left: int, right: int) -> int:
    return ((left % right) + right) % right


def rot4_code(code: int) -> int:
    return py_mod(code - 97 + 4, 26) + 97


def encrypted_char(code: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    guards = [code < 97, 97 <= code <= 122, code > 122]
    assert sum(guards) == 1
    if guards[0] or guards[2]:
        return (code,)
    return (rot4_code(code),)


def encrypt_fold(accumulator: tuple[int, ...], suffix: tuple[int, ...]):
    current = accumulator
    remaining = suffix
    descent = []
    while remaining:
        descent.append(len(remaining))
        current = current + encrypted_char(remaining[0])
        remaining = remaining[1:]
    assert all(a > b for a, b in zip(descent, descent[1:]))
    return current


def final_loop_char(suffix: tuple[int, ...], initial):
    current = initial
    remaining = suffix
    while remaining:
        current = (remaining[0],)
        remaining = remaining[1:]
    return current


def main() -> None:
    text = VERIFICATION.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    declarations = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip().startswith("syntax ")]
    rules = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip().startswith("rule ")]
    assert len(declarations) == 5
    assert len(rules) == 9
    assert text.count("[function, total]") == 5
    assert "<k>" not in text and "</k>" not in text
    for forbidden in [
        "simplification",
        "priority",
        "concrete",
        "owise",
        "no-evaluators",
        "fresh",
        "#Exists",
        "#Forall",
    ]:
        assert forbidden not in text, forbidden

    for code in range(-10000, 10001):
        result = encrypted_char(code)
        assert len(result) == 1
        if 97 <= code <= 122:
            assert 97 <= result[0] <= 122
            expected = 97 + ((code - 97 + 4) % 26)
            assert result[0] == expected
        else:
            assert result[0] == code

    assert [rot4_code(code) for code in range(97, 123)] == [
        ord(char) for char in "efghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcd"
    ]
    sample = tuple(map(ord, "`az{"))
    assert encrypt_fold((), sample) == tuple(map(ord, "`ed{"))
    assert encrypt_fold(tuple(map(ord, "P:")), sample) == tuple(
        map(ord, "P:`ed{")
    )
    assert final_loop_char((), "prior") == "prior"
    assert final_loop_char(sample, "prior") == (ord("{"),)

and reaches `.K` with the exact closure still bound and `result` equal to
`str(encryptResult(S))`. It additionally constrains scope allocation, heap,
heap allocation, stack, return state, and exception state to normal final
values. The omitted exit-code cell is framed and the program has no exit
operation.

### Mechanical pinning

The reviewer checker
[program_pinning.py](evidence/program_pinning.py) removes whitespace only
outside K String tokens and extracts balanced constructor terms. It established:

- trusted regeneration equals submitted `solution.mpy`;
- the sole submitted `FuncDef` constructor has digest

- the first constructor inside the entry claim's loaded `Module` is byte-for-
  byte the same normalized constructor with the same digest;
- the only remaining loaded constructor is exactly

- the target closure contains the exact same body once, at definition scope 0;
- the postcondition contains exactly one
  `"result" |-> str(encryptResult(S))` binding and no entry precondition.

a substituted implementation or a free summary. See
[04-program-pinning.log](evidence/04-program-pinning.log).

Every Python `str` is representable as a finite `IntSeq` of code points. The
model admits additional integer sequences too, so this is a superset rather
than a narrowing. Although supplied `Str(String)` source literals and `chr`
are ASCII-limited, every program literal is ASCII and the guarded arithmetic
can call `chr` only with 97 through 122. Arbitrary input code points are carried
symbolically and take the pass-through branch. Therefore there is no supplied-
model representation gap on the source-contract domain.

[04-witness-substitution.log](evidence/04-witness-substitution.log). In

code 98 (`"b"`) and cannot meet the unchanged ROT4 code-97 (`"a"`) result.

[05-rule-inventory.md](evidence/05-rule-inventory.md), generated by

Every submitted constructor is declared: `Module`, `FuncDef`, `Params`,
statement sequencing, `Expr/Str`, `Assign`, `For`, `If`, `BoolOp`, `Compare`,
`CmpOp`, `Call`, `Name`, `Int`, `AugAssign`, `BinOp`, and `Return`. The actual

- module/function/builtins scope lookup and ordinary closure call frames;
- one-time iterable evaluation and structural string iteration;
- target binding to the current scope;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write deterministic SHA-256 manifest for final audit artifacts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path("/audit-output")
EVIDENCE = ROOT / "evidence"
OUTPUT = EVIDENCE / "MANIFEST.sha256"


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main() -> None:
    paths = [ROOT / "REVIEW.md"]
    paths.extend(
        path
        for path in sorted(EVIDENCE.iterdir())
        if path.is_file() and path != OUTPUT
    )
    lines = []
    for path in paths:
        relative = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
        lines.append(f"{digest(path)}  {relative}")
    OUTPUT.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"manifest_entries={len(lines)}")
    print(f"manifest_path={OUTPUT}")
    print(f"manifest_sha256={digest(OUTPUT)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
